articles.title: A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer's -- and scientists found a way to block it
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental Alzheimer's compound prevented damaging protein clumps from forming in mouse brains and was linked to longer nerve-cell survival and reduced amyloid buildup. The findings are preclinical and also reported effects on heart health and some aging-related measures.

articles.title: A little movement in midlife could pay off for your brain years later
articles.summary_3_sentences: Exercise and healthy blood sugar levels in midlife were associated with slower cognitive decline later in life. The report noted especially strong apparent benefits of physical activity among Mexican American adults.

articles.title: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells release the stress hormone CRH near damaged brain tissue. The signal appeared to influence how these cells mature and rebuild nerve insulation, with possible implications for brain development and stress-related psychiatric risk.

articles.title: Immune cells flood into the aging brain, Stanford scientists discover
articles.summary_3_sentences: Stanford researchers reported that immune cells from the blood enter the aging human brain in substantial numbers, beginning as early as middle age. Some of these cells may transform into microglia-like brain immune cells, challenging older assumptions about brain immune isolation.

articles.title: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer's in their brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a study of more than 21,000 participants, women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life had lower odds of dementia and Alzheimer's-related brain changes. The reported associations included fewer amyloid plaques and tau tangles at autopsy, but the summary does not establish causality.

articles.title: Human brain cells are far more powerful than scientists thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that individual human cortical neurons can perform complex computations. The finding suggests single brain cells may contribute more to human cognitive abilities than simple on-off signaling models imply.

articles.title: The adult brain can repair itself better than scientists thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, researchers identified astrocytes that respond to brain injury by rebuilding damaged cellular networks. The cells created new nuclei and moved them through long extensions to help repopulate injured regions, making the work preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain rhythm that could improve Parkinson's treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a brain network and electrical rhythm that may underlie the benefits of deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease. The discovery could support more precise and individualized stimulation settings.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain has a fast lane and slow lane for clearing waste
articles.summary_3_sentences: AI-assisted measurements showed that fluid moves quickly around the brain's outer spaces but much more slowly through deep tissue. The finding may help researchers study waste-clearance problems linked to aging, Alzheimer's disease, and concussion.

articles.title: Exercise may help the aging brain "take out the trash"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that regular exercise may support the brain's glymphatic waste-clearance system. The proposed mechanisms include better sleep, reduced inflammation, and healthier blood vessels, all relevant to aging brain health.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain shift that begins around age 50
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that around age 50, the brain's memory center may lose many resident immune cells and gain more inflammatory ones. The shift may help explain how normal aging increases vulnerability to dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term brain study linked smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids with vascular dementia-related brain damage. The findings suggest that modifying vascular and lifestyle risk factors could delay or reduce some dementia-related changes.

articles.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Vanderbilt researchers developed a selective inhibitor of TAOK-1, a protein linked to Alzheimer's disease, and also found a compound that activates the TAOK protein family. The compounds are research tools that may help uncover disease mechanisms and possible treatment strategies.

articles.title: Scientists may have found aging's hidden trigger for brain disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: In worms, the protein EPS8 accumulated with age and promoted signaling tied to toxic protein clumping, neuronal damage, and shorter lifespan. Reducing EPS8 activity prevented harmful aggregates and preserved nerve function in this model system.

articles.title: AI can tell if your brain is aging faster than you are
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used machine learning on EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults to estimate whether the sleeping brain looked older than expected. A higher estimated brain age was associated with substantially greater dementia risk.

articles.title: Scientists discover why poor sleep may harm some brains more
articles.summary_3_sentences: A gene involved in overnight brain cleaning may influence how strongly poor sleep relates to Alzheimer's-linked brain changes. The finding points toward prevention strategies that consider both genetics and sleep habits.

articles.title: Scientists discover how obesity may fuel Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers described a possible pathway connecting obesity with Alzheimer's disease through fat molecules that reach the brain and disrupt immune defenses. Correcting the fat imbalance improved memory and brain function in Alzheimer's models, making the evidence mechanistic and model-based.

articles.title: Genomic Mapping Opens a New Frontier in Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that genomic mapping is opening a new frontier in Alzheimer's research. The available summary indicates that the work uses genetic or genomic approaches to study Alzheimer's disease mechanisms.

articles.title: Eating within 8 hours may help keep the aging brain sharp
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small six-month trial, older women who limited eating to roughly 8 to 9 hours per day performed better on planning and problem-solving tests than those eating over a longer window. Both groups lost similar weight, suggesting meal timing may have independent cognitive relevance.

articles.title: A hidden Alzheimer's tipping point may decide who gets dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a possible tipping point that may determine whether Alzheimer's brain changes progress to dementia. The proposed factor involves how brain immune cells respond to plaques and tau, suggesting a target for cognitive resilience research.

articles.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that SuperAgers did not simply have fewer Alzheimer's-related genetic risks than typical older adults. Their preserved memory may instead reflect still-unknown protective influences involving the brain, body, lifestyle, or environment.

articles.title: APOE2 may protect the brain from Alzheimer's and aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The APOE2 gene, linked to longevity, appeared to protect brain cells by reducing DNA damage and supporting neuronal recovery from stress. The finding may guide efforts to mimic APOE2's protective effects in people at higher Alzheimer's risk.

articles.title: Lab-grown mini brains may predict which Alzheimer's treatments will work
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patient-derived brain organoids showed differing responses to an antidepressant in Alzheimer's-related tissue models. The organoids and released particles may eventually help personalize treatments and improve disease diagnosis, but the work remains model-based.

articles.title: Watching too much TV in midlife may shrink the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: In about 1,700 adults, frequent television viewing in midlife was linked to smaller later-life brain regions involved in memory, decision-making, and visual processing. The summary notes that sedentary time alone did not explain the pattern, as mentally engaging seated work showed healthier brain associations.

articles.title: Alzheimer's breakthrough: Scientists restore two hours of sleep without clearing brain plaques
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice with amyloid plaques, overactive microglia promoted inflammation and reduced deep restorative sleep. Temporarily removing most microglia restored more than two hours of sleep per day without clearing plaques, making the finding preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists discover a protein that protects the brain from Alzheimer's damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: A protein called SORLA reduced tau accumulation, brain atrophy, and synaptic damage in mouse models. The study also pointed to a possible drug target involving harmful activity in supporting brain cells.

topic_groups.topic: Mental Health, Sleep, Cognition, and Behavior

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years -- the screen time result was unexpected
articles.summary_3_sentences: An eight-year Finnish study found that children with more screen time tended to show better cognitive processing as teenagers. Researchers suggested that context matters, including physical activity and screen activities that involve learning, creativity, or active thinking.

articles.title: Common food preservative linked to rising suicide deaths among young people
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that a widely available food-preservation chemical is linked to rising suicide deaths in the UK, especially among younger people and men. They called for restrictions on access and harmful online information, while noting the scale may be underestimated.

articles.title: THC Drug Reduces PTSD Nightmares
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that dronabinol, a prescription form of THC, reduced PTSD-related nightmares. The visible summary says it lowered both nightmare frequency and intensity.

articles.title: Why your brain keeps making the same decisions - even when better options exist
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that repeating a decision can reshape preferences, making familiar choices feel better than alternatives. The brain may rely on memory of prior choices instead of evaluating every option anew, helping explain habits and seemingly irrational decisions.

articles.title: Ozempic may have revealed the brain's hidden "craving center"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ozempic-like drugs may reduce cravings for alcohol and other addictive substances as well as hunger. Researchers are focusing on the lateral septum, a GLP-1 receptor-rich brain region that may connect reward memories with compulsive pursuit.

articles.title: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
articles.summary_3_sentences: MIT researchers reported evidence that language and logical reasoning rely on separate brain systems. People with severe stroke-related language impairments solved logic puzzles comparably to controls, and language-processing regions were largely quiet during reasoning tasks.

articles.title: A daily glass of fruit juice was linked to lower depression scores
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small four-week trial, adding a daily glass of 100% fruit juice or a smoothie to a healthier diet was linked to lower depression scores. The finding is preliminary and does not show that juice alone treats depression.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their "stress hormone" already elevated
articles.summary_3_sentences: Frequent cannabis users were reported to wake with elevated cortisol levels, suggesting altered daily stress rhythms. Researchers raised questions about whether using cannabis for stress relief could disrupt stress-regulation systems over time.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: A seven-day intensive meditation retreat was linked to changes in brain and body measures related to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and pain relief. Participants also showed connectivity patterns resembling those seen with psychedelic experiences.

articles.title: Stress can scramble your brain's internal GPS, MRI study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that cortisol impaired navigation in a virtual environment and disrupted activity of grid cells that help encode spatial location. When landmarks were missing, this navigation system nearly stopped functioning, while another brain region appeared to compensate.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Teens who began using cannabis showed slower growth in memory, attention, language, and processing speed. The summary identifies THC as the likely driver, especially for worsening memory trajectories.

articles.title: Wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: A wearable ultrasound patch helped 28 participants reach REM sleep faster and remain there longer. The device was also associated with signs of improved stress regulation and changes in emotion-related brain circuits.

articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: A prescription THC medication reduced recurring trauma-related nightmares in people with PTSD. More than one-third of participants reported that nightmares disappeared after ten weeks, according to the summary.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary_3_sentences: In rats, orexin neurons helped sustain effort when rewards became harder to obtain. Blocking these neurons weakened motivation, making the finding relevant to basic research on goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary_3_sentences: Participants who sat upright reported more pride and took more successful risks in a virtual decision-making task than those who hunched. The study suggests posture may modestly influence mood and decisions, though the effects should not be overstated.

articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes Christof Koch's work on whether the brain creates consciousness or whether consciousness may be more fundamental. It discusses unresolved questions including near-death experiences and terminal lucidity.

articles.title: Your gut may help your brain decide what to remember
articles.summary_3_sentences: In rats, nutritious foods strengthened memory-related brain activity more than sweet liquids with little nutritional value. Blocking the vagus nerve erased this effect, suggesting gut-brain signaling helps link meals with memory in animals.

articles.title: Your dreams aren't random. Your brain is rewriting reality
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large study of more than 3,700 dream and waking reports found that dreams are shaped by personality and surroundings. The dreaming brain appeared to combine memories, emotions, imagined possibilities, and familiar settings rather than simply replaying daily events.

articles.title: Magic mushrooms may reshape the brain long after the trip ends
articles.summary_3_sentences: A single psilocybin dose produced measurable brain activity changes and possible structural changes lasting up to a month. Participants with greater increases in flexible brain activity also reported more insight and later well-being improvements.

topic_groups.topic: Nutrition, Metabolism, Obesity, and the Microbiome

articles.title: When gut microbes run low on fiber, they may start eating you
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that when fiber is scarce, gut microbes may consume proteins from the protective mucus lining of the gut. Fiber suppressed this process, while indigestible plant proteins helped microbes produce more beneficial compounds.

articles.title: Scientists solve the mystery of a brain "switch" that can trigger weight loss in opposite ways
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, activating the GIP receptor in the brainstem reduced appetite, while blocking it in the hypothalamus removed a brake on fullness signals. The work may help explain why different GIP-targeting obesity drugs can produce similar weight-loss effects.

articles.title: Full-Fat Dairy May Be Healthier Than Previously Thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that full-fat dairy may be healthier than previously thought. It says avoiding full-fat dairy may not be necessary, challenging some prior dietary recommendations.

articles.title: Drinking orange juice every day may change thousands of genes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Regular orange juice consumption was reported to influence genes tied to inflammation, blood pressure, metabolism, and blood sugar control. The summary also cites possible cholesterol, vascular, and microbiome benefits, with citrus compounds such as hesperidin proposed as contributors.

articles.title: A surprising brain discovery could help explain why we overeat fatty foods
articles.summary_3_sentences: A protein inside appetite-controlling brain cells may help prevent overeating and obesity when high-fat foods are available. The report also notes male-female differences that could affect obesity risk and responses to weight-loss drugs.

articles.title: This common vitamin deficiency becomes far more dangerous when paired with belly fat
articles.summary_3_sentences: In more than 5,500 adults over 50, abdominal obesity combined with vitamin D deficiency was linked to a 123% higher risk of death over six years. Each factor was associated with risk individually, but the combination appeared especially concerning.

articles.title: Pill-Based GLP-1 Drug Cuts Weight by Up to 12.1%
articles.summary_3_sentences: Aleniglipron, a pill-based GLP-1 drug, helped adults with obesity or overweight lose up to 12.1% of body weight over 36 weeks. The article focuses on an oral alternative to injectable GLP-1 treatments.

articles.title: How Plant-Based Foods Boost the Gut Microbiome & Human Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines how plant-based diets affect microorganisms in the gut. It links plant-based foods, the gut microbiome, and potential benefits for human health.

articles.title: New GLP-1 pill delivers up to 12% weight loss in 36 weeks
articles.summary_3_sentences: The experimental oral GLP-1 drug aleniglipron helped people with obesity or overweight lose up to 12.1% of body weight over 36 weeks. The small-molecule pill can be taken once daily and may be easier to produce at scale than injectable drugs.

articles.title: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
articles.summary_3_sentences: Indigenous Peruvians were reported to carry high numbers of a starch-digestion gene, likely shaped by the rise of potatoes as a staple food. The genetic shift began thousands of years before European contact and supports the idea that diet can shape human evolution.

articles.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study finds a surprising health divide
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 340,000 adults found that heavy drinking increased mortality risk regardless of beverage type. At lower levels, beer, cider, and spirits were linked to higher mortality, while wine was associated with lower risk, including lower cardiovascular mortality among moderate wine drinkers.

articles.title: For decades, we were told to choose low-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a 12-week study, adults eating three servings of full-fat dairy daily did not show meaningful increases in weight, body fat, cholesterol, or insulin resistance. They also had improved blood pressure and higher intake of calcium, protein, and vitamin D.

articles.title: Cutting sweet foods doesn't curb cravings or improve health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-month trial found that high-, low-, and average-sweetness diets did not meaningfully change sweet preferences, body weight, or diabetes and heart-disease markers. Many participants drifted back toward prior eating habits after the trial.

articles.title: Why the Loss of Some Fat Cells Can Lead to Diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines why losing some types of fat cells can be linked to diabetes. It notes that while fat is often viewed negatively, some fat cells are important for healthy metabolism.

articles.title: Your brain may be wired to regain lost weight
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains that the brain may defend a previously higher body weight by increasing hunger and cravings and reducing energy use after weight loss. It also notes that drugs such as Wegovy and Mounjaro can reduce appetite signals, though effects may fade when treatment stops.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome is Linked to Memory Formation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that the gut microbiome is linked to memory formation. It describes new research suggesting that gut microbes may influence a process usually attributed primarily to the brain.

articles.title: Ozempic in a Pill? Oral GLP-1 Drugs Show Promise in Mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Newer oral drugs related to Ozempic reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice. The finding is preclinical and focuses on oral GLP-1 approaches and reward-linked feeding behavior.

articles.title: Specific Gut Microbes Linked to Changes in Aging Rates
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that specific gut microbes are linked to changes in aging rates. It frames the gut microbiome as an influential factor in human health and well-being.

articles.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain's food craving circuit
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, newer oral drugs related to semaglutide reduced pleasure-driven eating by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The preclinical finding could inform research on cravings and possibly substance use disorder.

articles.title: The billion-dollar problem keeping Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound from patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that GLP-1 drugs may offer strong health value but could overwhelm insurance budgets if provided to all eligible patients. The article also warns that low-cost compounded versions may carry safety risks.

articles.title: Coffee may protect your heart but energy drinks could harm it
articles.summary_3_sentences: An American Heart Association review found that up to 400 mg of caffeine per day, roughly three to five cups of black coffee, is generally safe for most adults and may be linked to lower cardiometabolic risks. Highly concentrated energy drinks and shots, however, can raise blood pressure and trigger irregular heart rhythms.

articles.title: Artificial Sweeteners May Impair the Growth of Gut Microbes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that artificial sweeteners may impair the growth of gut microbes. It frames the finding in the context of the microbiome's role in human health.

articles.title: Coffee may help the body fight stress and aging through a hidden cellular switch
articles.summary_3_sentences: Compounds in coffee appeared to activate NR4A1, a receptor involved in cellular protection from stress, inflammation, and damage. The reported protective effects disappeared when the receptor was removed, and plant compounds such as caffeic acid seemed more active than caffeine.

articles.title: Popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults with the highest intake of several artificial sweeteners showed faster declines in memory and thinking, especially if they were under 60 or had diabetes. Researchers stressed that more studies are needed before concluding that sweeteners cause cognitive decline.

topic_groups.topic: Cardiovascular, Kidney, Mobility, and Musculoskeletal Health

articles.title: Scientists reveal why walking gets so much harder with age
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that older adults may stiffen the ankle more during walking, trading efficiency for stability. This could contribute to shorter strides, slower walking, and fatigue, while balance and lower-leg strength exercises may help preserve mobility.

articles.title: This 10-cent heart drug cuts hospitalizations by 25%
articles.summary_3_sentences: Low-dose digoxin, an inexpensive older heart drug, was reported to reduce heart-failure hospitalizations by about 25%. The finding could support renewed attention to digoxin in heart-failure care.

articles.title: The common mistake that could make aging joints hurt more
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article warns that avoiding movement may worsen aging-related joint problems. Low-impact activity such as swimming, cycling, tai chi, yoga, and walking may nourish cartilage, strengthen protective muscles, and reduce osteoarthritis pain.

articles.title: Taking the stairs could protect your heart and help you live longer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis of more than 480,000 people found regular stair climbing was associated with lower cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Stair climbers also had lower reported risks of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure.

articles.title: 1 in 5 people may carry this hidden genetic heart risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: In more than 20,000 people, very high inherited Lp(a) levels were linked to greater risk of major cardiovascular events, especially stroke and cardiovascular death. The article notes that Lp(a) can be detected with a blood test and may be missed by standard cholesterol testing.

articles.title: Scientists find the strength training "sweet spot" for a longer life
articles.summary_3_sentences: People who performed about 90 to 120 minutes of strength training weekly had a lower risk of early death in the reported study. Combining strength training with aerobic exercise was associated with an even larger reduction in overall mortality risk.

articles.title: Scientists reveal how much exercise you really need to protect your heart
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large study suggested that 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous exercise per week may provide only modest protection from heart attack and stroke. Substantially greater benefits were reported around 560 to 610 minutes per week.

articles.title: A drug already used for osteoporosis blocked spinal damage in a new study
articles.summary_3_sentences: Zebrafish with a faulty collagen-related gene developed spinal mineral buildup and fusion resembling human disc disease. Researchers reduced damage using an existing osteoporosis drug and by targeting fat metabolism, making the evidence preclinical.

articles.title: Dirty air may trigger painful rheumatoid arthritis flares
articles.summary_3_sentences: Fine pollution particles from smoke, soot, and dust were linked to worsening rheumatoid arthritis and higher risk of flares, especially after prolonged exposure. The findings suggest air-quality avoidance may be relevant to disease management.

articles.title: Simple Weekly Workout Improves Cardiovascular Fitness and Weight Loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that one longer exercise session per week may improve cardiovascular fitness and weight loss. The visible summary says results may be comparable to several shorter sessions.

articles.title: Scientists may have found a way to prevent statin muscle pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified an immune response that may help explain statin-associated muscle pain, weakness, and exercise intolerance in some people. The finding could eventually lead to ways to protect muscles while preserving cardiovascular benefits.

articles.title: Popular Childhood Drinks May Cause High Blood Pressure Later in Life
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that sugary drinks consumed during childhood may be linked to high blood pressure later in life. The visible summary focuses on long-term health effects of childhood beverage intake.

articles.title: A daily fiber supplement reduced knee arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary_3_sentences: A prebiotic fiber supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain in a six-week trial and also improved grip strength and pain sensitivity. The results suggest a possible gut-muscle-pain connection.

articles.title: Exercise may not help hip arthritis as much as patients expect
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major review found that exercise produced only small average improvements in hip osteoarthritis pain and physical function. Researchers noted that exercise may still help some people, but evidence is limited on which approaches work best.

articles.title: Natural compound may fight rheumatoid arthritis at its source
articles.summary_3_sentences: A plant-derived compound reduced swelling, inflammation, and joint damage in rats with rheumatoid arthritis. It also affected immune balance and fat processing, making the finding preclinical.

articles.title: Finerenone Delays Kidney Function Decline
articles.summary_3_sentences: Finerenone was reported to slow kidney function decline and reduce serious kidney complications. The article also states that the drug reduces serious cardiovascular complications in the studied population.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Diseases, Vaccines, and Antimicrobial Resistance

articles.title: COVID-19 awakens dormant viruses -- and one is linked to long COVID
articles.summary_3_sentences: COVID-19 was reported to reactivate dormant viruses including Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and herpes viruses. One poorly understood viral family was strongly associated with long COVID and lasting disability.

articles.title: Immune Cell Reprogramming Eliminates the Need to Treat Poultry with Antibiotics
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that immune cell reprogramming could eliminate the need to treat poultry with antibiotics. The finding is framed around reducing antibiotic use in chicken production.

articles.title: A surprising triple treatment completely clears hiv in newborn primates
articles.summary_3_sentences: In newborn nonhuman primates treated within three days of exposure, a combination of antiretroviral drugs, broadly neutralizing antibodies, and leronlimab cleared HIV. None of the treatments worked alone, and the finding remains preclinical.

articles.title: Moderna's mRNA Flu Vaccine Wins FDA Approval
articles.summary_3_sentences: Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine mFlusavia received FDA approval. The article identifies the product as an mRNA vaccine for influenza.

articles.title: A New Strategy to Tackle Drug-Resistant Gonorrhea
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a new strategy for tackling drug-resistant gonorrhea. The approach may also be adaptable to other bacterial pathogens that resist existing drugs.

articles.title: Pediatric Antimicrobial Resistance
articles.summary_3_sentences: A JAMA Pediatrics study reported that antimicrobial resistance in children is increasing globally. The article frames the trend as a pediatric and global health concern.

articles.title: A Working Antibacterial Resistance Gene is Found in Nature
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that an active antibacterial resistance gene was found in nature. It highlights antibiotic resistance as a growing problem in which bacterial pathogens can evade drug treatment.

articles.title: WHO Begins Trial for Ebola Outbreak
articles.summary_3_sentences: The WHO began a trial during an Ebola outbreak involving Bundibugyo virus disease. The article notes that there are currently no approved treatments or vaccines for this disease.

articles.title: Novel Bacterial Strains are Implicated in Urinary Tract Infections
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that novel bacterial strains are implicated in urinary tract infections. It broadens attention beyond E. coli, a common bacterial cause of UTIs.

articles.title: A new antiviral could stop measles before an outbreak takes off
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental pill prevented a measles-like virus from spreading through air or close contact in ferrets. It worked when given shortly before or after exposure and reduced illness and contagiousness, making the evidence preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists revive a powerful antibiotic that superbugs had defeated
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers paired vancomycin with a small molecule called pghi-4 that blocks a bacterial resistance-related enzyme. The combination restored activity against drug-resistant E. faecium in the reported work.

articles.title: New molecular map reveals how the flu virus hijacks human cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists mapped how influenza A commandeers human cells, including a strategy that dissolves nuclear structures and releases proteins the virus may use to reproduce. The map may reveal drug targets and help study dangerous strains such as H5N1.

articles.title: A Novel Pathway Boosts COVID-19 & Drives Lung Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a newly identified pathway boosts COVID-19 and drives lung damage. It links this pathway to worsening effects of SARS-CoV-2 in the lungs.

articles.title: This food compound may help vaccines work better in older adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small pilot trial, spermidine supplements after a third COVID-19 vaccine dose appeared to improve immune responses in adults over 65, especially initial poor responders. The reported improvements included higher antibodies and stronger activity against several variants.

articles.title: Common antidepressant may ease long COVID's crushing fatigue
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a randomized trial of 399 adults, fluvoxamine significantly reduced long COVID fatigue and improved quality of life compared with placebo. The article describes it as one of the first medications to show meaningful benefit for this symptom.

articles.title: Air Pollution Alters Health Measurably Before Lung Cancer Diagnosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that air pollution alters health measurably before lung cancer diagnosis. The visible summary frames lung cancer as a major global and U.S. health issue.

articles.title: A simple blood test could detect multiple cancers and reveal where they started
articles.summary_3_sentences: UCLA researchers developed a blood test that scans DNA signals for multiple cancers, liver diseases, and signs of organ damage. Early results suggest it may also indicate where disease is developing, but the summary frames the work as preliminary.

articles.title: A protein older than blood circulation could transform cancer immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that tumor-produced C3 can block immune-suppressing cells and improve immunotherapy response. Recreating the effect improved survival in mice with resistant tumors, making the evidence preclinical.

articles.title: Vitamin C may fight cancer -- but not the way scientists once thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article contrasts ineffective vitamin C pills with intravenous vitamin C, which reaches much higher concentrations and may behave more like an experimental cancer drug. Early studies suggest possible cancer-cell damage, fewer side effects, and improved outcomes for some patients, but evidence remains developing.

articles.title: Chewing Gum Reduces HPV, Cancer-Linked Bacteria
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that chewing gum made from lablab beans dramatically reduced HPV. It also says the gum nearly eliminated two bacteria linked to head and neck cancer.

articles.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Shows Efficacy for Pediatric Sarcoma
articles.summary_3_sentences: An antibody-drug conjugate showed efficacy for pediatric sarcoma, according to the article. The summary highlights Ewing sarcoma as an aggressive bone cancer representing about 1% of pediatric cancers.

articles.title: Cancer-fighting chewing gum cuts HPV levels by up to 93%
articles.summary_3_sentences: A specially engineered chewing gum reduced HPV by up to 93% and nearly eliminated two bacteria linked to head and neck cancer. The treatment reportedly preserved beneficial oral bacteria and may offer a lower-cost approach.

articles.title: A common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
articles.summary_3_sentences: Chemotherapy-surviving ovarian cancer cells may release fructose that helps neighboring tumor cells loosen, escape, and spread. The article notes that implications for sugary diets and cholesterol-lowering drugs have not yet been confirmed in patients.

articles.title: A simple supplement could help the immune system fight cancer and viruses
articles.summary_3_sentences: Low arginine levels were reported to reduce production of a cellular warning protein, potentially helping cancer cells and viruses evade immunity. In mice, arginine-rich diets were linked to fewer colon tumors and milder viral infections, making the therapeutic evidence preclinical.

articles.title: Aggressive Bladder Cancer Outcomes Improve with Addition of Immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports improved outcomes for aggressive bladder cancer when immunotherapy was added to treatment. It focuses on muscle-invasive bladder cancer, described as a significant clinical challenge.

articles.title: New cancer strategy could stop tumors before resistance takes hold
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are using evolutionary theory to change cancer treatments before tumors develop resistance. Mathematical models suggest rapid, carefully timed switches among therapies could improve cure rates.

topic_groups.topic: Drug Discovery, Approvals, Biomaterials, and Regenerative Medicine

articles.title: Scientists turn sheep's wool into a material that helps regrow bone
articles.summary_3_sentences: Keratin extracted from sheep's wool helped damaged bone regenerate in animals. The resulting tissue was more organized and structurally similar to healthy bone than tissue grown with conventional collagen scaffolds, making the finding preclinical.

articles.title: Using Jellyfish Bycatch for Marine Collagen Production
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study explored using jellyfish bycatch to produce marine collagen. The work examines whether an often-caught marine byproduct can be converted into a useful biomedical or industrial material.

articles.title: FDA Approves First-in-Class Narcolepsy Drug
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Takeda's oveporexton, marketed as Orzeyful, for adults with narcolepsy type 1. The article describes it as a first-in-class narcolepsy drug.

articles.title: Two deadly flowers could inspire powerful new medicines
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified six enzymes used by wolfsbane and larkspur to produce the complex compound atisinium. They recreated the pathway in tobacco plants, offering a possible sustainable route to produce and test rare medicinal molecules.

articles.title: Study Explores Potential Drug Treatment for Cholestatic Itch
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature Chemical Biology study investigated a small-molecule inverse agonist targeting an itch receptor. The research explored a potential drug treatment for cholestatic itch.

articles.title: Cone Snail Venom in Development of Non-opioid Painkillers
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study examined a peptide derived from cone snail venom for pain reduction. The peptide is being considered for development as a non-opioid painkiller.

articles.title: Psychedelics Gain Momentum in Big Pharma
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports growing pharmaceutical interest in psychedelics, highlighted by Eli Lilly's $2.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley. It suggests the deal may encourage other companies to enter the field.

articles.title: Study Examined The Effectiveness of Antibody Injection Simulations
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters examined antibody injection simulations. The article describes a computer model used to predict aspects of antibody injection behavior.

articles.title: Can Virtual Humans Transform Drug Discovery?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes Deep Origin's use of in silico drug testing with virtual humans. The approach aims to help researchers avoid experiments likely to fail and improve drug discovery efficiency.

topic_groups.topic: Environmental, Climate, Space, and Exposure Science

articles.title: Scientists detect a surprising shift in human blood as atmospheric CO2 rises
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers analyzing more than two decades of U.S. health data found rising blood bicarbonate levels and declining calcium and phosphorus levels that tracked increasing atmospheric CO2. The study suggests atmospheric change may leave measurable signals in human physiology.

articles.title: Marine heatwaves are harming human health in surprising ways
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers warned that marine heatwaves can affect human health by intensifying storms, triggering harmful algal blooms, reducing seafood supplies, and disrupting livelihoods. The article also notes mental health impacts such as anxiety, grief, and depression in coastal communities.

articles.title: Scientists discover bacteria that lock toxic uranium into a stable form
articles.summary_3_sentences: In uranium-contaminated mine water, microbes fed with glycerol removed about 95% of dissolved uranium within 130 days. The bacteria helped convert uranium into an unusually stable compound, suggesting possible bioremediation relevance.

articles.title: Spaceflight Linked to Accelerated Aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that long-term spaceflight is linked to accelerated aging. It cites a GeroScience study focused on how extended time in space may affect aging processes.

articles.title: Scientists tracked 12 people in Antarctica for 10 months--what happened could shape future Mars missions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A ten-month Antarctic experiment found that frequent contact among a small crew was linked to tension and mistrust, not just loneliness. The crew increasingly divided along cultural and language lines, offering lessons for future Mars missions.

articles.title: World's most-used weedkiller disrupts honeybee brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that glyphosate-exposed honeybees foraged 13% less after three days and showed changes in brain chemicals linked to behavior. At hive scale, such effects could reduce honey production, weaken pollination, and threaten colony survival.

articles.title: The Power of Bacteria: Cells Render Uranium Inert
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that bacterial cells can render uranium inert. It frames the finding as an example of microbial adaptation to diverse and challenging environments.

topic_groups.topic: Genetics, Evolution, Paleontology, and Ancient Biology

articles.title: A 60-year-old theory about ants, bees and wasps may be wrong
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis challenged the idea that an unusual genetic system alone explains the evolution of complex social colonies in ants, bees, and wasps. Researchers suggest other insect traits may be central to eusocial evolution.

articles.title: Neanderthal gene linked to more muscle mass in modern humans
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that a Neanderthal-derived gene is linked to higher muscle mass in some modern humans. The association applies only to some people carrying the inherited variant.

articles.title: Paleontology rocked by organic molecules found in 66-million-year-old dinosaur bones
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported strong evidence that original collagen can persist in dinosaur fossils for tens of millions of years. The finding could provide molecular clues about dinosaur biology and protein preservation.

articles.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists studying early life found evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged twice. The work suggests life may share an ancient genetic code while having undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

articles.title: 3,500-year-old skeletons challenge what scientists thought they knew about syphilis
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ancient remains from Vietnam suggest yaws-like diseases may have been transmitted from mother to child thousands of years ago. The finding complicates how researchers interpret ancient infections and the origins of syphilis.

articles.title: For 15,000 years, humans and dogs have been changing each other
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes how dogs and humans have shaped each other over about 15,000 years. Dogs adapted to diverse environments and roles, including sledding, hunting, high-altitude life, wool production, and ceremonial functions.

articles.title: Scientists find unexpected life on Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-year-old body
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified ancient and modern microorganisms on Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-year-old body. They separated microbes from his lifetime from those arriving after death, including traces of gut bacteria and cold-loving yeasts.

articles.title: Forget the sperm race: Fertilization may depend on teamwork
articles.summary_3_sentences: An evolutionary study found that sperm cooperation is widespread among arthropods and has repeatedly emerged and disappeared over hundreds of millions of years. The finding challenges the simple idea that fertilization is only a race among individual sperm.

articles.title: Scientists catch a "jumping gene" mid-leap between species
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found circular intron RNA from a predatory bacterium inside dead cells of another microorganism. Because the RNA forms a stable ring, it may provide a previously unknown route for mobile genetic elements to move between species.

articles.title: Scientists found two mysterious 'ghost' ancestors hiding in our DNA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Modern humans were reported to carry DNA from two extinct lineages in addition to Neanderthals and Denisovans. The finding suggests human evolution involved repeated mixing among multiple human groups.

articles.title: Scientists found evolution repeating itself in the Galápagos Islands
articles.summary_3_sentences: Galápagos giant daisies repeatedly evolved similar heat-tolerant leaf shapes through different gene combinations. Researchers also found genetic differences among isolated populations, suggesting speciation may be underway.

articles.title: Hidden genetic diversity helped inbred brown tree snakes conquer guam
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-read sequencing uncovered more than 19,000 large genetic differences in brown tree snakes, many in genes tied to immunity and smell. This hidden diversity may have helped a small founding population survive inbreeding and invade Guam successfully.

articles.title: Scientists trace the shocking origin of human eyes to an ancient "cyclops"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers suggested that a tiny one-eyed ancestor from nearly 600 million years ago shaped the evolution of vertebrate eyes. They also linked its ancient median eye to the modern pineal gland, which helps synchronize sleep with daylight.

articles.title: Scientists discover the hidden brain switch that assigns bees their jobs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified bee brain circuits that help determine age-related colony jobs. When the circuits were switched off, older worker bees resumed caring for the queen rather than performing later-life roles.

articles.title: Scientists found mystery bacteria inside one of the ocean's most elusive whales
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found three previously unknown Helicobacter bacteria in pygmy sperm whale stomachs. All four infected whales showed serious digestive damage, but the bacteria were not confirmed as the cause of death.

articles.title: One faulty gene copy can make the heart's DNA fold the wrong way
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that losing one copy of TBX5, a gene linked to congenital heart disease, can disrupt the 3D folding of DNA in heart cells. The cell-to-cell variability may help explain why people with the same mutation can develop different heart defects.

articles.title: Dogs can tell fear from sadness -- and scientists saw it in their brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Brain scans showed that happy human faces activated regions in dogs associated with higher-level processing and reward. The findings suggest human smiles may carry special emotional significance for dogs.

articles.title: Study Documented Creation and Analysis of Super-sized Starch Granules
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists from the Seung group at the John Innes Centre created wheat-derived starch with large granules. The study documented the creation and analysis of these super-sized starch granules.

articles.title: New autism therapy shows surprising benefits even in adult mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Blocking the glycine transporter SLC6A20 restored brain signaling and improved social, communication, and repetitive behaviors in autism-related mouse models. The treatment also worked in human brain organoids and showed lasting effects in adult mice, making the evidence preclinical and model-based.

articles.title: Unexpected Roles for a Muscle-Protecting Protein are Revealed
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports newly identified roles for TRF2, a protein known for protecting chromosome ends. The finding suggests TRF2 has additional functions relevant to muscle protection.

articles.title: Genetic Study of Fibromyalgia Reveals a Surprising Link to Huntington's
articles.summary_3_sentences: A genetic study of fibromyalgia reported a surprising link to Huntington's disease. The article describes fibromyalgia as a disorder involving fatigue, widespread sensitivity, aches, and pain.

articles.title: Allergy-Reducing Bacteria are Identified
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports identification of bacteria that may reduce allergies. It links the finding to the farm effect, in which rural microbial exposure is associated with lower allergy risk in children.

articles.title: Scientists find a simple way to stop cavities without drilling
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major U.S. trial found that silver diamine fluoride stopped decay in more than half of treated baby teeth. The treatment is brushed on without drilling, shots, or sedation, but permanently darkens decayed areas.

articles.title: Single Drug Dose Reversed Autism-Like Traits in Mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that one dose of rapamycin temporarily reversed autism-like brain dysfunction and behavior in adult mice. The finding is preclinical and involved an immunosuppressant drug.

articles.title: Surprising Variation in Individual Gene Expression is Discovered
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports surprising variation in gene expression between individuals. It notes that blood samples often provide only a snapshot of gene activity.

articles.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, mild inflammation during pregnancy led offspring to develop persistent brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors, and increased seizure risk. A single rapamycin dose improved many of these problems within about two hours, but the benefits were temporary and preclinical.
